text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The vice-president of right wing Disy party Nicos Anastassiades declares his decision to run for party president is irrevocable.
- The United States decides within three to four weeks on how to exercise their influence on the Cyprus issue.
- The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees is pulling out of Cyprus after 23 years.
- The British bases deny reports of imminent release of a youth jailed for traffic offences.
- Finance minister can only see prosperity in Cyprus. Christodoulos Christodoulou attacks party leaders and media bosses for their criticism on the outlook of the economy.
- The United Nations is preparing a package of measures to improve the climate in Cyprus during proximity talks. Mediators remain silent on the process.

- Controversy over the proposed pay rises to senior state officials continues. The chairman of the house finance committee, who has opposed the pay rise, did not show the same sensitivity when MPs got a wage hike, says the finance minister.
- A Turk accused of spying on national guard positions was conveying his information to Turks living in the mixed community village of Pyla.
